'''Ikatsu no Mikoto''' (中臣 烏賊津) is a legendary noble and regarded as the founder of the {{ill|Nakatomi clan|ja|中臣連}} from the {{ill|Kofun period|en|Kofun period|qid=Q459939|lt=Kofun period}}. Although not mentioned in the *{{ill|Kojiki|en|Kojiki|qid=Q813031|lt=Records of Ancient Matters}}*, he is referred to in the *{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Chronicles of Japan}}* under various names such as '''Nakatomi no Ikatsu Omimi''' and '''Rai Daijin no Mikoto'''. Genealogical texts such as *{{ill|Sonpi Bunmyaku|en|Sonpi Bunmyaku|qid=Q1704738|lt=Sonpi Bunmyaku}}* identify him as the son of Omi Sayama no Mikoto and father of {{ill|Ōkogashi no Mikoto|ja|大小橋命}} and {{ill|Iki no Makoneko|ja|真根子命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maneko no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22125699}}.

== Records ==

According to the *{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Chronicles of Japan}}* (vol. 8), upon the sudden death of {{ill|Emperor Chūai|en|Emperor Chūai|qid=Q179971|lt=Emperor Chūai}}, {{ill|Empress Jingū|en|Empress Jingū|qid=Q232803|lt=Empress Jingū}} kept his death secret with the help of senior officials, including {{ill|Nakatomi no Ikatsu|ja|中臣烏賊津}}, {{ill|Otomoneshi no Mikoto|ja|大三輪大友主|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Ōmiwa no Ōtomonushi|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q55536810}}, and others. Ikatsu no Mikoto was tasked with protecting the court during this period.<ref>*{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Chronicles of Japan}}, Emperor Chūai, year 9, February 5 entry.</ref>

Later, in vol. 9 of the *Chronicles*, Empress Jingū chose Ikatsu no Mikoto to perform sacred divinations (審神者) during her preparation for an important ritual.<ref>*{{ill|Nihon Shoki|en|Nihon Shoki|qid=Q813935|lt=Chronicles of Japan}}, Empress Jingū, pre-regency record (Emperor Chūai, year 9, March 1 entry).</ref> His role as a mediator between gods and humans is emphasized, reflecting the meaning of the term "Nakatomi."

Subsequent records in the reign of {{ill|Emperor Ingyō|en|Emperor Ingyō|qid=Q349258|lt=Emperor Ingyō}} mention a courtier named Nakatomi no Ikatsu Omimi, who is believed by some scholars to either be a different person with the same name or the same individual as Ikatsu no Mikoto.<ref>*{{ill|Sonpi Bunmyaku|en|Sonpi Bunmyaku|qid=Q1704738|lt=Sonpi Bunmyaku}}</ref>

== Tsushima Legends ==

Several legends about Ikatsu no Mikoto are preserved on {{ill|Tsushima Island|en|Tsushima Island|qid=Q52051|lt=Tsushima Island}}:<ref>Tsuzuki Tōzō, *Shinto in Tsushima* (San-Ichi Shobō, 1972).</ref>
* {{ill|Raijin Shrine|ja|雷神社}} in Izuhara Town commemorates Ikatsu no Mikoto as the figure who managed foreign tribute after returning from Silla.
* {{ill|Raimyo Shrine|ja|雷命神社}} in Izuhara is linked to his descendants.
* {{ill|Tai Norito Shrine|ja|太祝詞神社}} in Mitsushima Town is believed to house his grave.
* {{ill|Hekireki Shrine|ja|霹靂神社}} marks the place of his arrival from Silla.
* {{ill|Norito Shrine|ja|能理刀神社}} is where he is said to have performed divinations.

== Genealogy ==

Ikatsu no Mikoto is identified as the son of {{ill|Omikiyama no Mikoto|ja|臣狭山命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Omi Sayama no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q99517230}}. His children include {{ill|Ōkogashi no Mikoto|ja|大小橋命}}, {{ill|Iki no Makoneko|ja|真根子命|12=simple|13=User:Immanuelle/Maneko no Mikoto|comment=changed title based on wikidata|qid=Q22125699}}, and {{ill|Nihon Daijin no Mikoto|ja|日本大臣命}}. Some accounts mention his marriage to a woman from Baekje or Silla, with their descendants linked to several prominent clans.<ref>*{{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|en|Shinsen Shōjiroku|qid=Q1045362|lt=Shinsen Shōjiroku}}</ref>
